claims.text: The initial material is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes extensive oxidation in high-temperature air.
A thin, uniform, adherent alumina coating can be deposited on HfNbTaTiZr by chemical vapor deposition.
The applied coating will form a stable, adherent alumina layer on the alloy surface.
The dense alumina layer will act as an oxygen-diffusion barrier.
Retarding oxygen ingress will prevent rapid oxidation of the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
The alumina coating process and subsequent exposure will not alter the bulk microstructure responsible for the alloy's mechanical performance.
At 1000 °C in air for several hundred hours, coated samples will exhibit lower oxidation mass gain than uncoated samples.
At 1000 °C in air for several hundred hours, coated samples will develop thinner or less detrimental oxide layers than uncoated samples.
After coating and high-temperature exposure, room-temperature tensile ductility will remain within or similar to 8–16%.
After coating and high-temperature exposure, yield strength at 1000 °C will remain within or similar to 163–530 MPa at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The proposed operating boundary is steady air at 1000 °C for exposure times on the order of hundreds of hours.
Performance may vary with coating method, coating thickness, and cyclic thermal loading.
Long-term coating adhesion under cyclic thermal stress and the coating's effect on fatigue performance are uncertain.
The coating process could alter the near-surface microstructure and localized mechanical properties.
